title: Whether trust is an act of faith
pass_a_gloss: Article XVIII. Whether trust is an act of faith. 1. Orthodox theologians do not speak of trust in the same way. Some hold trust to be the justifying act of faith itself; others that it is an act distinct from faith though inseparable; others that trust is taken in several ways. 2. Trust can be taken: (1) as firm persuasion of God's mercy in Christ; (2) as resting on God's promises; (3) as courageous opposition to dangers and miseries; (4) as joy and peace of conscience concerning remission already obtained. 3. We with most of the Orthodox: justifying trust is an act of faith — or rather justifying faith essentially includes trust, by which Christ and the promises of grace are applied to us. It is not mere historical knowledge, nor bare dogmatic assent. 4. Bellarmine's view — that trust of certainty concerning particular remission cannot be had in this life without special revelation — is rejected: Scripture exhorts the faithful to trust, and gives signs to the regenerate by which they are made certain of their participation in Christ.
pass_b_english: Article XVIII. Whether trust is an act of faith.
1. Orthodox theologians differ on trust: some identify it with faith's justifying act; some call it distinct but inseparable; some take trust in several senses.
2. Trust may mean: firm persuasion of God's mercy in Christ; resting on his promises; courageous stance against dangers and miseries; or joy and peace of conscience over remission already obtained.

3. With most Orthodox: justifying trust is an act of faith — or justifying faith essentially includes the trust by which Christ and grace's promises are applied to us. Not mere historical knowledge or bare dogmatic assent.
4. Bellarmine's claim that certainty of particular remission needs special revelation in this life is rejected. Scripture urges trust and gives the regenerate signs of their share in Christ.
source_text:
ART. XVIII.
An fiducia sit actus fidei.

1. Theologi Orthodoxi non eodem modo loquuntur de fiducia. Alii fiduciam esse ipsum fidei actum justificantem; alii eam esse actum a fide distinctum, etsi inseparabilem; alii fiduciam pluribus modis accipi.

2. Fiducia accipi potest: (1) ut firma persuasio de DEI misericordia in CHRISTO; (2) ut recumbentia in DEI promissis; (3) ut animosa oppositio contra pericula & miserias; (4) ut gaudium & pax conscientiae de remissione jam impetrata.

3. Nos cum plerisque Orthodoxis: fiducia justificans est actus fidei — seu potius fides justificans essentialiter includit fiduciam, qua CHRISTUS & promissiones gratiae nobis applicantur. Non est mere notitia historica, nec nuda assensio dogmatica.

4. Bellarmini sententia, fiduciam certitudinis de remissione particulari non posse haberi in hac vita absque revelatione speciali, rejicitur: Scriptura fideles hortatur ad fiduciam, & signa regeneratis dat quibus de sua in CHRISTO participatione certi reddantur.
